quest.title: Shade Upon Red Silk
quest.description: One day, you and Paimon stop by the Grand Bazaar...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x525, Mora x34075, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, Paimon's trying to remember... what else did we put on our shopping list...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sniff* Oh, what a mouthwatering smell! Paimon would know the aroma of Biryani anywhere! Let's go get some!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That wasn't on our list, was it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, we can still add it to the list!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: #Well, if it isn't {NICKNAME} and Paimon. Wasn't expecting to see you here.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Hello there! It's been quite a while.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so you two are still hanging out together! Dehya, didn't you say last time that you were gonna head back to the desert?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Haha, I said I was going to resign from being her bodyguard, not that our friendship was over. We're still the best of friends.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: The Homayanis also still post jobs from time to time. Their pay is always generous, so me and the other mercs never pass them up.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: I told Dehya to just stay at our place when she took one of those jobs a few days ago.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: My parents were delighted. They even said that it always felt like we were missing someone whenever Dehya wasn't around.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Pff, that sounds like something they would say alright. They are always so welcoming...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Anyway, the job is already taken care of, so I was gonna head back to the brigade as soon as I finished a little shopping. But the master kept insisting and I ended up staying for another day.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: You can stay for as many days as you want, Dehya. Father hasn't even gotten around to treating you to his best dishes yet.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Heh, you know I'm not the kind of person to stay put in one place like that, my lady. Don't worry though — there'll always be next time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But she said they'll treat you to the "best dishes"... Paimon can't believe you can still refuse that!

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Ah, but wait, didn't you say last time that you would take me on a trip to the desert? Why don't you just take me with you today when you leave?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: There are so many places I still haven't visited yet.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, my lady, but no can do. There are still a few things I need to take care of back at the brigade. Besides, the desert hasn't exactly been the most peaceful place lately.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Oh, come on, not this again! That's also what you said last time, and the time before that.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I know, I'm sorry! Just give me some more time, and I promise I'll plan the best trip ever for you.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Alright, fine. To be perfectly honest, it's not that I wanted to go, it's more like... I feel like something is off about you lately.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Ever since you first set foot on the estate a few days ago, you've been acting anxious and even paranoid.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Have you been delaying our trip because you've run into some kind of trouble?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Nah, are you kidding? You're worrying too much.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Would you swear on that? Friends shouldn't lie to each other, you know. I won't pry any further if you're willing to swear on what you just said.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: But if something really is bothering you, then just tell me. You know I'll help you however I can.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, looks like Dunyarzad was on to something.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: *sigh* You're too perceptive, my lady. Seems I can't hide anything from you.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I just thought that nothing good could come out of telling you about the messy happenings of mercenaries. Knowing too much only leads to more trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Mercenary life is a dog-eat-dog world where Mora reigns supreme. Everything operates on a completely different set of rules.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: That doesn't change anything about what I just said, though. We're still friends, and I can only support you if I understand what's bothering you.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: My lady... *sigh* You're not gonna stop until you drag it out of me, are ya...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Alright, I'll share what I know. Let's go somewhere else first, this isn't exactly the best place for a discussion.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Okay, let's talk here. Just try not to draw any extra attention.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: As you may already know, the Eremites have both a lot of mercenaries and a complex organizational structure. Many mercs are no different than me, just going around looking for jobs to earn some Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: My brigade is called the "Blazing Beasts." We're not a large group, but every member is loyal and brave.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: However, not all Eremite brigades are like mine. Some are willing to cross all kinds of lines for the sake of Mora. The most notorious is a faction known as "Deshret's Relics."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Deshret's Relics? Judging from the name, they must really look up to...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Yep, you got it. I've heard that you've already crossed paths with Ayn Al-Ahmar? They're one of the groups under the Relics' banner.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, you mean the group that tried to sell us the Divine Knowledge Capsule! Yeah, they weren't friendly at all...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Deshret's Relics is composed of many smaller brigades like Ayn Al-Ahmar. The Relics' headquarters issues orders to all brigades under its control.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: On any other day, I would want nothing to do with them. Unfortunately though, the brigade that's stirring up trouble now is none other than Dakan Al-Ahmar.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Dakan...?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I think it means "beard" or something. Believe me, it's a really stupid name... I've found it insufferable for years.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Anyway, the real issue is that Dakan Al-Ahmar is led by my father, Kusayla.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Say what now!?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: I think I'm starting to understand your anxiety now... but what did they do?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I won't go into details, my lady, but they've been involved in a lot of violent incidents. We're talking hundreds.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Hundreds!?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Yep. The scenes tend to be quite gruesome, too. They strip the victims of all their valuables before murdering them.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Not only have they targeted merchant caravans and ordinary citizens, but other mercenary brigades as well.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: ...That's beyond terrible. They won't even spare their own kind.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I don't know how Deshret's Relics sees it, all I do know is that Dakan Al-Ahmar has become more and more aggressive over the last few years.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: If I don't do something about them, then even my brigade or the people of Aaru Village could become their next target.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: *sigh* I just wish I knew what's driven him to do this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, how can your father do such terrible things?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I dunno, people change. He's always been pretty pathetic, but at least in the past, there were still a few lines that he wouldn't cross.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's setting the bar pretty low...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I mean, if he was even remotely decent, then why would I have to leave the brigade and cut all ties with him?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: He was loud and foolish, with no real sense of purpose. Instead of doing anything useful, he spent most of his time drinking and chasing after women.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Of course, the other brigade members were just like him. Their ruckus would go on night after night...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like a nightmare...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: What about your mother? Did she ever step in to stop them?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: ...Unfortunately, I never knew my mother.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Ah... I'm sorry, Dehya. I didn't know...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: It's alright, my lady. That's pretty common in mercenary circles. Didn't I mention that my father was chasing after women? I was the result of one of those encounters with some random person.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: He told me that he wasn't sure who my mother was, and in any case, she never came to see me.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: He'd say, "You'll be fine as long as you remember to stick with Dad," but even then, he left most of the parenting to the brigade. The one thing I do remember is that he used to tell me stories.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: But the problem was that he had terrible taste. He only knew a few stories, and even those tended to be pretty stale...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: They were tales of desert warriors defeating dragons in the forest, or stories of mercenaries rescuing princesses from rebel armies.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like your typical fairy tales...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: More or less, yeah. They were interesting maybe the first or second time around, but after about 20 repeats, they started to get a little dull...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: He seemed to think those stories were the best things ever, though. He was so into 'em that he'd call the whole brigade over and make them perform the whole thing as a play.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Even the toys he gave me would all be story props... I'd get helmets, shields, and toy swords.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: It was only much later when I realized that the shows were more for him than they ever were for me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...What an interesting guy.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But it doesn't sound like he had all bad intentions?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Yeah, I've always found him pretty childish, but that was something I could just shrug off. I had no reason to despise him...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: ...Until I grew up, and learned the true face of Deshret's Relics for myself.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Looting, blackmail, violence, and fraud... They not only accepted such heinous acts, they would even openly boast about them.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: No one in the brigade was any kind of hero, instead, my father and his cronies were more like the bad guys that needed to be taken down.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Did they really think that as long as they didn't do any of that stuff right in front of me, I would never know?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: I think I can understand your feelings. The difference between perception and reality must have hit hard...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Yeah, but don't worry, my lady, it's all water under the bridge to me now. I had a huge argument with my father, and left that place behind for good.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I'm not investigating them due to any bitter feelings I still have towards my father. I just want to protect those that are close to me.

choices.text: You just want to find out...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Yeah, I told the boys to gather as much information as they could. Most of the reports concern violent incidents, but there's also some talk of smuggling.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: I see... But isn't this investigation incredibly dangerous?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: It is, but every mercenary lives life on the edge. It's a lifestyle that I enjoy.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: That may be true, but it'll be impossible for those who care about you not to worry.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Well... now you get why I didn't want to share any of this with you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What should we do? They both have valid concerns...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll go back to the desert with Dehya.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Huh? But there's no need for you to get caught up in this mess, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, {M#he}{F#she}'s super tough, so if {M#he}{F#she} went to the desert with you, then Paimon bets the problem would be solved in no time!

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: #Hmm... I'm inclined to agree. I'd feel a lot more at ease if you took {M#him}{F#her} along to help.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: I'll wait for news from you in the city until then. Please, stay safe.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I'm honored that you care so much for me, my lady.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Alright, then let's get moving. Our first stop will be Caravan Ribat, where we can catch up a bit with my fellow mercs.

choices.text: Why they suddenly started causing so much more trouble.

talks.objective: Go to Caravan Ribat to learn more about the situation

dialogues.speaker: Harun
dialogues.text: Hey, Dehya, you're back! Are these two friends of yours?

choices.text: It's a pleasure to meet you.

response.speaker: Harun
response.text: Hahaha, likewise. There's no need to be so formal with us. We're a pretty casual crew.

response.speaker: Harun
response.text: Anyway, since we've got newcomers, let me fill you in on what Dakan Al-Ahmar's been up to lately.

response.speaker: Harun
response.text: They've become extremely aggressive. Apparently even their own now have become acceptable targets.

response.speaker: Harun
response.text: They even attack other Relics brigades just the same as any other mercenary brigade.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Even the most ferocious beasts still protect their own. It sounds like they've thrown that straight to the wind.

response.speaker: Harun
response.text: That's right. Once they've collected enough loot off the other mercenaries, they sell it off to a different brigade, or turn to merchants on the black market.

response.speaker: Harun
response.text: A portion of their profits is immediately exchanged for more food and weaponry to be used in their next violent operation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's terrible...

response.speaker: Harun
response.text: Yeah, and it really makes you wonder why they're so desperate for Mora.

response.speaker: Harun
response.text: A few days ago, Hisham and I trailed them for a while, and even disguised ourselves as merchants to conduct trade with them. We were able to learn a few things from the exchange.

response.speaker: Harun
response.text: Rather than saying they're out to plunder and hoard Mora, it'd probably be more accurate to say that they're experiencing an internal power struggle.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Wait, a power struggle?

response.speaker: Harun
response.text: You heard me right. The vast majority of their victims are mercenaries from the other brigades of Deshret's Relics.

response.speaker: Harun
response.text: If their only goal was Mora, they could have gone after anybody. The targeted nature of their attacks points to a power struggle between the different brigades within the Relics, that's the only plausible explanation we have.

response.speaker: Harun
response.text: Unfortunately, we weren't able to find out anything more specific. It seems they're also trying to keep things under wraps.

response.speaker: Harun
response.text: Oh, one last thing we discovered was that over the past few years, as Dakan Al-Ahmar became more and more active, Deshret's Relics as a whole became a lot weaker.

choices.text: They were able to cause so much damage...?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Sounds mighty strange to me, too. Harun, you can leave the rest of the investigation to us.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Gotta say though, I didn't expect you to go on a whole undercover mission during the few days I was gone. Sounds like you were really putting your necks on the line, no?

response.speaker: Harun
response.text: Nah, it was nothin'. We're just as concerned about the situation as you are. Dakan Al-Ahmar is your father's crew, after all.
Haha, what he said. Besides, Dehya, haven't you done more dangerous things than all of us combined? What we did is nothing compared to your experiences.
Yeah! And while they went to talk with Dakan Al-Ahmar, I took a look at the last camp they attacked.
Any survivors of the attack were already long gone. There was nothing of value left in the camp.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Ah, Hisham and Khalaf, you're here too.

response.speaker: Hisham
response.text: We rushed over as soon as we saw you come into Caravan Ribat.

response.speaker: Hisham
response.text: #Although this new friend of yours looks a little green behind the ears, I'm sensing a special vibe from {M#him}{F#her}.

response.speaker: Hisham
response.text: Now that we know you'll have a capable partner with you, we can also rest easy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, what about Paimon? Feel anything special?

response.speaker: Hisham
response.text: Oh, uh... You're also planning to tag along with them?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Of course! Paimon is the Traveler's most important guide. Wherever {M#he}{F#she} goes, Paimon will follow!

response.speaker: Hisham
response.text: Oh, in that case... then you'd better take care of her too, Dehya.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, don't underestimate Paimon!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Hahaha, don't worry about her. She may look tiny and helpless, but she's been through just as many battles as the Traveler here.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Even if she had only survived on sheer luck, then that alone would still make her quite formidable.

response.speaker: Hisham
response.text: Hah, I had no idea... I guess I shouldn't judge by appearances, haha.

response.speaker: Khalaf
response.text: Oh, one other thing, Dehya. When you're free, why don't you update the deputy about your upcoming schedule?

response.speaker: Khalaf
response.text: We held another recruitment event a few days ago, but everyone only came to see the Flame-Mane. You weren't around at the time, so people were pretty disappointed to only find our crew of rough, unkempt guys.

response.speaker: Khalaf
response.text: The deputy put a lot of effort into the event, but it was basically for nothing... only a few people chose to stay, and that really got to him.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Ah, sorry to hear that. I'll be sure to bring him some great liquor next time... I left in a hurry, and I couldn't make it back in time for the event.

response.speaker: Hisham
response.text: Gotta admit, I can understand their disappointment, though. You're our brigade's main selling point, after all.

response.speaker: Hisham
response.text: Now, if only the deputy could figure out a way to bring a few more smokin' hot members into our ranks...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Hah, keep dreaming. Remember the last time I invited a couple gals into the brigade? You all just froze up with your mouths gaping, like a bunch o' scarecrows.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: The awkward silence and weird expressions left quite the impression on 'em. They were originally interested in joining us, but after that, they both told me they were too uncomfortable to stick around.

response.speaker: Hisham
response.text: Hey, didn't we agree to never bring that up again!?

response.speaker: Khalaf
response.text: Huh? Wait, are you serious? Why've I never heard about this?

response.speaker: Harun
response.text: I don't think you were a part of the brigade yet.

response.speaker: Khalaf
response.text: Are you kidding me!? I missed a once-in-a-lifetime moment like that, and you weren't even gonna tell me!?

response.speaker: Harun
response.text: Alright, alright! We can tell you about it later. Now's not the time.

response.speaker: Khalaf
response.text: Hey, don't you try to change the subject! You and Hisham get your butts over here and tell me everything right now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, are they... always like this?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Haha, more or less.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: There aren't many rules or graces when it comes to mercenaries. We're used to just speaking our minds.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: If someone starts getting under your skin, you just yell right back at 'em. If that doesn't put an end to it... eh, then you just challenge 'em to a fight.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: But we also don't tend to take many things too seriously. Being direct and getting it all out of your system as soon as things come up is better than keeping everything bottled up and never talking about it.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: That's also why I never spare their feelings when I talk to them. If I wanna laugh, I'll laugh. If I'm angry, then I'll unload on 'em. It's hard to stop once you get used to it, though I can never do that when I'm with the Homayanis.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Hey, knuckleheads. Can you at least tell me the rest of the intel before you go back to your bickering?

response.speaker: Harun
response.text: Yeah, you hear her, Khalaf? Told ya we gotta focus on the investigation first. Ahem, I drew up a map — right here's the spot — there you'll find the merchant caravan responsible for getting rid of Dakan Al-Ahmar's looted goods.

response.speaker: Harun
response.text: All you gotta do is wait and ambush them in the evening. They'll have no idea what hit 'em.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Perfect, thanks for that. Be sure to pass my regards to everyone else in the brigade as well.

response.speaker: Harun
response.text: Will do. You stay safe, Dehya.

choices.text: That somehow makes things even more confusing.
I'd trust Dehya with my life.

response.speaker: Harun
response.text: Oh? So you've already become like one of us then, haha. That's good to know.

talks.objective: Watch over the trade route and wait for your moment

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: This should be the place. Let's find a spot to hide and bide our time.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: It's gonna come down to a fight one way or another, so let's all be careful.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #No need to worry! {M#He}{F#She} knows {M#his}{F#her} way around a fight.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Haha, I'm not worried about that! What I meant is that we probably shouldn't go too hard on the enemy. After all, we still need to get information out of them.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Ah, here they come! You ready?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Let's not give them a chance to react and end this quickly.

talks.objective: Intercept the caravan and search for clues

dialogues.speaker: Sattar
dialogues.text: A—Argh!

dialogues.speaker: Sattar
dialogues.text: Y—You're... the Flame-Mane!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Good, that saves me an introduction. Alright, time for a little talk. Are you buddies with Dakan Al-Ahmar now? Tell me, what're they after?

dialogues.speaker: Sattar
dialogues.text: Hmph... You know the code of being a mercenary just like everyone else. The first rule is to never divulge key information about our employer. What makes you think I'd talk?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Heh, that might have worked on an amateur, but I know you're just looking to protect your reputation.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Think about it, though. What's your reputation worth if you won't have the other tools you need to succeed in this line of work? Tools like, I dunno... your limbs, or eyes?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: You've got five seconds. You might want to think twice about how much your employer's information is worth to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—Whoa!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I'm not joking around. We can do this the easy way, or the painful way.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Two seconds...

response.speaker: Sattar
response.text: I'll save you the trouble... Hmph!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Huh!? Are you crazy!?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: He tried to bite off his own tongue! Quick, search the area for any first aid supplies!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: With Dehya's emergency treatment, the bleeding in Sattar's mouth is brought under control...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Ugh, I definitely didn't expect him to go that far. Thankfully, the wound wasn't too deep, and he just passed out from the pain.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But why would he be so extreme...?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I just wanted to test his mettle. You can get a lot of mercenaries to talk just by threatening them.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I didn't expect him to be willing to go through so much pain just to deny us some intel.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, he's out cold for now... We could wait for him to wake up, but maybe it's not a good idea to interrogate him any further... What should we do?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Yeah, don't worry about it. It'll be a waste of time to interrogate him again after that. He might just hurt himself again if we start asking.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: There are lots of goods around here. Let's search the area, maybe we'll be able to find something.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: ...I'm really sorry.

talks.objective: Look for clues among the goods

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We found a piece of paper with a bunch of names on it! Maybe it's a record of something?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Lemme take a look. If this really is a merchant caravan, they should have a record of their transactions.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hmm... Yep, I see an entry for Dakan Al-Ahmar right here. Kusayla, Idrisi, Bashar, and Tikriti...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: All familiar names. Dakan Al-Ahmar has been trading for a hefty supply of food, weapons, and medicine. It seems that in the past, they used to receive some Canned Knowledge as well.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: This caravan is just one link in their logistics chain. Once in the rainforest, the caravan will exchange the looted goods for Mora, and the funds will then be passed to a specific person.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: That person will then pack the caravan full of necessary goods, which will then be brought right back to Dakan Al-Ahmar...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...Wait. Why is there no Mora value recorded for the final transaction?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? No value?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Yeah. Every transaction before the last one was marked with an exact amount of Mora. But the final one, where they paid for everything to be brought back to the desert... was simply marked as "delivered."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe the Mora amounts just happened to cancel each other out?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hmm, perhaps, but they couldn't have known how much they would make off selling the loot. Do they not care about profit margins at all?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Anyway, the next part's the records of the goods themselves. There are a lot of entries... everything was probably sourced from the rainforest.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Shahzaman Homayani...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Homayani!? You mean Dunyarzad's family?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh, c—could it just be another family with the same last name?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I'd be surprised to find someone with the exact same first and last name. Shahzaman Homayani is Dunyarzad's father, and the head of the Homayani family.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Just what the heck is going on here...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I'm sorry... You're right. I'll consider what we've found, and not jump to conclusions just yet.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: But what this piece of paper confirms is that the Homayani family has been providing goods to Dakan Al-Ahmar.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What if the Homayanis have been kept in the dark, and don't know they've been trading with Dakan Al-Ahmar?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: That's a possibility, but if that was the case, why has this caravan specifically named Shahzaman as their person of contact?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: They could have just as easily bought goods such as food and medicine directly from Caravan Ribat or Port Ormos.

choices.text: If Shahzaman was actually aware of this...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Yeah... Funding violence and looting. The brigade gets the goods, and he is paid the proceeds from the sale of the loot.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: B—But why would he do something like this? It's not like the Homayanis are in need of money...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I honestly have no idea...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I've been to their estate many times, and I've never noticed anything suspicious.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: The only potentially large expenditure I can think of would be the treatment costs for Dunyarzad's Eleazar. Maybe they borrowed a lot of Mora in the past?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: But that's still just a speculation. I don't think the master would stoop so low to make Mora.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I don't think Dunyarzad knows anything about this, either.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: You're probably right. I know my lady's personality, and she wouldn't deliberately keep something like this from us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But what should we do now? All we've found is just another mystery...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: If we want to get to the bottom of this, we won't be able to turn back.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Hmm...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: If you ask me, we already have no choice but to confront her about this.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I'm not worried, it's too early to make a verdict yet. I still have faith in the Homayanis.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Let's go find my lady again. We'll tell her everything, and see if she's willing to lend us her support.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: If we're lucky, we can not only figure out the mystery of this paper, but also follow the trail of breadcrumbs to the people responsible at Dakan Al-Ahmar.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... Dehya, are you sure this is the best decision? What if instead of getting the help we need, we just end up revealing everything we've discovered to the enemy?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I've considered that possibility, but even still, I want to tell her what we've found. I think I owe her that much... True friendship is built on trust.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: She showed genuine concern for me when we first brought up the topic. I can't repay her kindness with doubt and suspicion.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: That's not how I deal with people.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're right. Paimon wants to trust Dunyarzad. too!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I hope we'll be of help to her.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Yeah. Let's pay another visit to Sumeru City.

choices.text: Then perhaps he's been supplying the brigade's operations this entire time.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Please be careful. I'll stay in the city and wait for news from you.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Just don't do anything reckless, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Harun
dialogues.text: Now, like I said... The two ladies Dehya brought with her were also like super-mercs, I'm talkin' same level as Flame-Mane here.

dialogues.speaker: Harun
dialogues.text: You should have seen it, the aura of the two of 'em when they were standing together... it was incredible! I was just at a loss for words, that's all!

dialogues.speaker: Khalaf
dialogues.text: So pathetic...

dialogues.speaker: Harun
dialogues.text: H—Hey, shut up!

dialogues.speaker: Observe
dialogues.text: (There are a lot of daily necessities like food and water in the boxes. It doesn't seem like there's anything noteworthy.)

dialogues.speaker: Observe
dialogues.text: (There are some weapons in the boxes, as well as a bunch of medicine and bandages. It seems like Dakan Al-Ahmar is really up to no good.)

dialogues.speaker: Observe
dialogues.text: (Sattar is not gravely injured, and will probably wake up soon. It should be okay to leave him here for a little while.)
